thread:
ryan (sales): Hey team — acme-edu POC next Wed. They want a two-region Dedicated pool (us-west + eu-west) and a short burst window for demo day. Baseline ~8 GPUs, burst to ~20 for ~4 hours. Can we do ephemeral cross-region burst + scoped dev keys?

priya (solutions): Confirming pricing/controls: reserved commits are monthly; burst usage should be billed on-demand. We can offer scoped hosted keys for devs, but dedicated pool access needs ACLs and allowlist. @leila any infra caveats?

leila (eng-ops): We can do a temporary autoscale override (burst credits + override) that won't permanently resize the pool. Need explicit start/end window and the model variant to pin so we avoid cold-start GPU pressure. Also need cloud quota check for eu-west.

mark (eng-infra): I can provision the split pool (rp-provision). Need: start/end ISO times, model to pin, and whether to enable prefix/KV caching for the demo. If you want, I can pin to a quantized variant to increase packing density.

ryan (sales): They plan 200 concurrent short evals (small context) and prefer q8_0 to keep mem down. Timeline: provision by Mon EOD, burst Wed 15:00-19:00 UTC. Also they want a few hosted API keys for their engineers to smoke-test before the demo.

priya (solutions): We'll create scoped hosted keys (dev-only) and a dedicated ACL for the POC team. Security will need to sign off on ephemeral VPC peering for the eu region. @nina any constraints?

nina (security): For POC we can allow ephemeral VPC peering and short-lived keys. Requirements: 1) log retention set to 30 days or less, 2) no PII persisted within logs/kv cache, 3) keys rotate after the demo window. We'll need the customer contact + IP ranges for the allowlist.

mark (eng-infra): OK provisioning plan. I'll create an autoscale override object and apply it to the pool namespace. Sample override I'll apply (exact fields used by runtime):

```
{
  "policy": "burst_override",
  "start": "2026-03-25T15:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-03-25T19:00:00Z",
  "baseline_gpus": 8,
  "max_gpus": 20,
  "model_pin": "acme-q8_0-v1",
  "kv_cache": "enabled"
}
```

ryan (sales): Perfect. Also need clarity on billing: will burst be charged against reserved commit if we don't have a commit? (customer asking about cost optimization).

priya (solutions): Short answer: burst/overage is billed at on-demand rate. If they want discounted rates we can discuss a short-term commit but not necessary for a 1-day demo. I'll include a cost estimate for the 4-hour burst.

mark (eng-infra): Starting provisioning now. Will post pool ids and scoped key names once done.

deploy-bot: pool-provisioner started provisioning request rp-8231 (regions: us-west, eu-west).

mark (eng-infra): rp-8231-us created, eu-west pending due to quota - pinging cloud team for +2 GPUs.

leila (eng-ops): Cloud quotas approved for eu-west, Mark — you should be able to finish create.

mark (eng-infra): Done — rp-8231-us and rp-8231-eu created. Applied autoscale override for 2026-03-25 15:00-19:00 UTC and pinned model to acme-q8_0-v1. Scoped hosted keys created: poc-acme-dev-abc123 (rotating). Dedicated ACLs and IP allowlist configured with customer ranges.

priya (solutions): Pricing note posted to the deal doc and shared with sales: burst billed at on-demand; no reserve required for this POC.

ryan (sales): Awesome — please drop the pool id + quick dev instructions. Need the hosted keys and a short playbook I can send to their SREs.

mark (eng-infra): Sharing: https://redwood.internal/poc/rp-8231/runbook — includes pool ids (rp-8231-us / rp-8231-eu), ACL steps, and how to use scoped hosted keys. I'll rotate keys immediately after the demo window.

ryan (sales): Thanks everyone :tada: This should cover demo day. We'll monitor latency/cost during the burst and follow up if they want a sustained commit afterwards.
